speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to examine you carefully; please describe the skin lesion you are concerned about, including its size, color, and any changes you've noticed over time. Also, have you experienced itching, bleeding, or pain in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of heavy smoking and non-healing lesions on both the penis and a digit, could you confirm if these areas have changed in size, shape, or color recently, and do you see any ulceration or bleeding?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Syphilis serology (RPR/VDRL)
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the information; the normal readings noted are noted but do not rule out local pathology. Given your heavy smoking history and the specific location of these non-healing, crusty lesions on the penis and finger, could you describe the texture of the lesions—specifically, do they feel indurated or ulcerated? Additionally, have you noticed any regional lymph node swelling in the groin or the hand?

REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Cutaneous).

The combination of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions on a heavy smoker's penis and finger, resistant to standard treatments for syphilis and eczema, is highly suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma. The normal blood work and serology rule out systemic infection but do not exclude localized malignancy. I will proceed with a biopsy of the penile lesion to confirm the diagnosis and staging.
